data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories inevitably smuggles induction back into Popper's system because any rationale for acting on past test results presupposes the uniformity of nature or the reliability of memory, which are inductive assumptions.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a non-inductive basis for action (e.g., convention, decisionism) can be coherently articulated without assuming future regularity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the definition of 'rationality' is restricted solely to logical consistency with past data, ignoring future application.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Reductio ad absurdum of the 'methodological rule': demonstrating that the rule 'prefer X' is irrational unless one assumes 'X is a reliable guide to future success,' which is an inductive claim.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
